title: NCPatcher file manifest
description: The ROM's NitroFS table after a build, with per-entry provenance. Written by files-dump, or by `ncpatcher rom files --json`. Consumers turn file ids into constants, or show what a project changes about a ROM.

variant.description: The variant this build produced. Absent when the run had no variant, which includes `rom files --json` reading a ROM off disk.

files.description: Every file in the table, not only the ones this run wrote: a generator naming files by id needs the whole table, and most of it is whatever the ROM already had. Sorted by id.

id.description: The FAT index, exactly as the ROM stores it. A game that offsets file ids at run time (NSMB subtracts its overlay count) applies that itself; it is a property of that game, not of the ROM. Existing ids are never renumbered by a build.

path.description: Slash-separated path inside NitroFS, with no leading slash. This is the name the file has now: an entry that claimed an id was renamed on the way in.

action.description: What this run did to the file, relative to the ROM that came in. `created` means the build appended it, which only happens under z_new/.

source.description: Where the bytes came from, relative to the project directory when the file is inside it. Present only when this run wrote the file, and absent for z_new/reserved, which NCPatcher creates out of nothing.

module.description: The module whose tree supplied the file. Absent for a project-level files: entry.

component.description: The component that names this destination in its files: patterns. Ownership only: a disabled component's files are subtracted before insertion, so nothing here is ever attributed to one.

from-variant.description: Which layer of a layered tree supplied the file: the built variant, or the base variant underneath it. Grouping by path across manifests answers which variants translate a file.
